items.example: Quería un café con leche, por favor.
items.example_en: I'd like a white coffee, please.
items.note: The imperfect used as a polite softener. Quiero is blunter but fine.

items.example: Un café solo y un vaso de agua.
items.example_en: An espresso and a glass of water.
items.note: solo means black, not alone, in a coffee order.

items.example: Para mí, un café con leche.
items.example_en: For me, a coffee with milk.
items.note: A cortado is an espresso with a splash of milk.

items.example_en: Two small beers, please.
items.note: The standard bar order in Spain, roughly 20cl.

items.example: Un zumo de naranja natural, por favor.
items.example_en: A fresh orange juice, please.
items.note: In Latin America: un jugo.

items.example_en: Could I have tap water?
items.note: agua is feminine but takes el in the singular, for the stressed a.

items.example: Con la caña ponen una tapa gratis.
items.example_en: They give a free tapa with the beer.
items.note: In parts of Spain it comes free with a drink; elsewhere you pay.

items.example: Una tostada con tomate y aceite.
items.example_en: A slice of toast with tomato and olive oil.
items.note: The classic Spanish breakfast.

items.example: ¿Para tomar aquí o para llevar? Aquí, gracias.
items.example_en: Eat in or take away? Here, thanks.
items.note: You will hear this at every counter.

items.example_en: Excuse me, the bill, please.
items.note: You have to ask; nobody brings it unprompted.

items.example_en: How much is that altogether?
Here you go, keep the change.
items.note: Tipping is modest in Spain; rounding up is normal.

items.example: Quería reservar una mesa para cuatro.
items.example_en: I'd like to book a table for four.

items.example: Buenas noches, ¿una mesa para dos en la terraza?
items.example_en: Good evening, a table for two on the terrace?
Could you bring us the menu, please?
items.note: Classic trap: el menú is a fixed-price set meal, la carta is the list of dishes.

items.example_en: What's in the set lunch menu?
items.note: Starter, main, dessert, bread and a drink for one price. The best value in Spain.

items.example_en: For the first course, a salad.
items.note: The set follows: el primero, el segundo, el postre.

items.example_en: Are you going to have dessert?

items.example: Para mí, el pollo, por favor.
items.example_en: I'll have the chicken, please.
items.note: The most natural way to order in a group.

items.example: Un filete al punto, por favor.
items.example_en: A medium steak, please.
items.note: The scale runs poco hecho, al punto, muy hecho.

items.example: Soy vegetariana, ¿hay algún plato sin carne?
items.example_en: I'm vegetarian, is there a dish without meat?
items.note: Feminine vegetariana.

items.example_en: I'm allergic to shellfish.
items.note: a plus el contracts to al.

items.example_en: Thank you, that was delicious.
items.note: The -ísimo ending is the everyday Spanish superlative.

items.example_en: Can we pay separately, please?
I do the shopping on Saturdays.
items.note: ir de compras means going shopping for pleasure.

items.example_en: Can you buy some bread?
items.note: No partitive article needed, unlike French.

items.example: Un kilo de tomates, por favor.
items.example_en: A kilo of tomatoes, please.
items.note: Also medio kilo, un cuarto.

items.example_en: These vegetables are in season.
items.note: las legumbres means pulses, not vegetables.

items.example_en: I buy fruit at the market.
items.note: Usually singular and uncountable, like English.

items.example_en: Is the fish fresh today?
items.note: estar because freshness is a condition, not an essence.

items.example: Compra los ingredientes de la receta.
items.example_en: Buy the ingredients for the recipe.
items.note: la receta means both a cooking recipe and a medical prescription.

items.example: Corta la cebolla en trozos pequeños.
items.example_en: Chop the onion into small pieces.
items.note: Recipes use the tú or usted imperative throughout.

items.example_en: Boil the pasta for ten minutes.
items.note: Stem-changing: cuece. Do not confuse with coser, to sew.

items.example_en: Add a pinch of salt.

items.example: Remueve bien hasta que quede suave.
items.example_en: Stir well until it's smooth.
items.note: False friend: it does not mean to remove, which is quitar.

items.example_en: It tastes slightly of lemon.
items.note: Same verb as to know, distinguished by the a and the context.
